prompt: Today more and more tourists are visiting places where conditions are difficult, such as the Sahara desert or the Antarctic. What are the benefits and disadvantages for tourists who visit such places?
essay:
In the modern day, places in harsh conditions are slowly becoming an attraction for many tourists.

Places such as the Sahara desert of the Antarctic are visited more and more. This essay discusses

the advantages and drawbacks for tourists who visit places that are in difficult conditions.

One primary benefit for people travelling to places with in conditions is that it can help them learn how to adapt in uneasy or uncomfortable situations. When visiting these types of places, many inconveniences could occur. For instance, the weather may be either too hot or too cold to get used to. This helps tourists learn how to be more flexible with harsh situations and adapt to them. To

illustrate, when I went to the Antarctic, it was extremely cold and hard to manage. However, after some time, I started to be able to manage the weather by understanding what I needed to wear.

As a result, this experience helped me with understanding how to adapt in harsh weather conditions.

However, there are also disadvantages for people who visit places in difficult conditions as well. One main drawback is that some places are overly dangerous for tourists. This could be because the area contains venomous animals, has extreme weather conditions, or has other factors. For instance, a rainforest may contain venomous snakes that could easily end a person's life. Though it is beneficial to learn how to adapt in different conditions, some places are too dangerous to risk our lives.

In conclusion, tourists travelling to places in harsh conditions have both merits and disadvantages.

Visiting these places can help us learn to adapt in difficult situations. Despite this, some places may be overly harsh for tourists to manage, which can be fatally risky.
